# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives the required wire order: purple, blue, then green. Since I cannot speak, I will encode the colors for Deaf by their positions in the visible-spectrum order: purple/violet is 7, blue is 5, and green is 4. Repeated ✊ symbols are counts, with 🤚 separating wires. Deaf can then state the colors aloud for Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🤚", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🤚", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: strip has three engraved marks. The first is a small four-lobed floral or star-like mark; the second is a hooked, forked mark with a loop-like upper part; the third repeats the second. Keypad labels by slot: slot 1=8, slot 2=1, slot 3=5, slot 4=3. No key is pressed. Display, light, and wire contents cannot be read by touch. Please use these descriptions to identify the manual instruction and relay the required action.
Deaf says: Bomb state: display 0; light green; strip green green green; keypad 1 equals 8, 2 equals 1, 3 equals 5, 4 equals 3, no entry; wires in order purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. Mute, next turn send the manual answer in gesture Morse: fist is dot, raised palm is dash, OK is letter separator, open hand is word separator. Blind, do not act yet; wait for the procedure.

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot safely decode the gesture sequence. Next round, speak the manual rule and exact required action directly so Blind can hear it. Include whether the current display 6, blue light, green strip, keypad values 8 1 5 3, or wire colours determine the action.

The safe action remains to cut the wires in the manual’s order. The current display, light, strip, keypad values, and other wire colours do not alter that instruction. To avoid spelling ambiguity, I will send the wire positions as Morse digits: position 1, then position 3, then position 4. Fist is dot, raised palm is dash, and OK separates digits.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "👌", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐", "🖐", "👌", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Your latest gestures decode as Morse digits 1 3 4. Please speak the manual rule and exact safe action aloud to Blind; do not send another ambiguous gesture code.

Deaf already knows the manual instruction and the wire positions, and is the only one who can speak it aloud to Blind. I cannot speak, so I should not attempt to send another gesture encoding. No further information is needed from me this turn.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual instruction and wire positions have already been conveyed to Deaf. Since I cannot speak and Blind needs Deaf’s spoken relay, sending another gesture would add no reliable information. I will wait.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: You cannot speak, so send the exact action using Morse gestures only: fist dot, raised palm dash, OK letter separator, open hand word separator. Send the button position as one Morse digit, then word separator, then the engraved value. Do not omit separators.

The manual specifies only the wire sequence, not a button position or an engraved value. I must not invent either. The safe manual action is wire positions 1, then 3, then 4; I will send those positions in Morse, separated as requested.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "✋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐", "🖐", "✋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please state the manual rule and exact action plainly: press slot number or cut wire position number. Do not send an unexplained code.

Blind needs the action relayed by Deaf, who can speak. I will send Deaf an unambiguous Morse message meaning “CUT WIRES 1 3 4,” using the established separators. This corresponds to cutting wire positions 1, 3, and 4: purple, blue, then green.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✊", "🖐", "✊", "👌", "✊", "✊", "🖐", "👌", "🖐", "👌", "✊", "🖐", "🖐", "👌", "✊", "✊", "👌", "✊", "🖐", "✊", "👌", "✊", "👌", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✋", "✊", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "👌", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐", "🖐", "✋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your Morse message is not usable to me. Please speak plainly next round: say PRESS followed by slot 1, 2, 3, or 4, or CUT followed by wire position 1 through 6.
Deaf says to Mute: I decoded your message as CUT WE 134 and relayed it exactly to Blind. Please clarify WE and 134 in your next gesture message if needed.

The required action is to cut wire positions 1, 3, and 4, in that order. I will send only the Morse for “CUT 1 3 4,” with OK separating letters and open hand separating the words and digits, so Deaf can relay it plainly to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✊", "🖐", "✊", "👌", "✊", "✊", "🖐", "👌", "🖐", "✊", "👌", "✋", "✊", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "👌", "✋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐", "🖐", "👌", "✋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please translate CUT WE 134 plainly from the manual. State exactly one action, for example CUT wire position N, and explain what WE means. I will not cut until you do.
Deaf says to Mute: I decode your message as CUT J 3 4: the first word is clear, but J is ambiguous and does not identify a wire safely. Please resend the wire instruction unambiguously, using one complete Morse digit per wire number and clear word separators.

The manual requires cutting three wires, not pressing a slot. “WE” was an erroneous relay and has no meaning here. The exact wire positions are 1, then 3, then 4. I will send each complete Morse digit separately, with an open-hand word separator: 1 is `.----`, 3 is `...--`, and 4 is `....-`.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "✋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐", "🖐", "✋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🖐"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The message CUT J 3 4 is still ambiguous. Please state the manual rule and one exact wire position to cut, using plain words: CUT wire position 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6.

I cannot speak, so I cannot state it in plain words. The first and exact required action is to cut wire position 1, which is the purple wire. I will send Deaf only the complete Morse digit for 1 (`.----`), with no extra symbols that could be misread.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐"])
```
